column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health check
The app ships the run manifest described in Deployment and answers the health check stated there, including while Kill Bill, Mailpit or MinIO is down.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables named in Configuration and secrets, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Same-origin server boundary
The server applies the request size limits, cross-origin refusal and never-served paths stated in Server boundary.

One error shape and precedence
Every API error uses the error shapes and the single precedence order stated in API.

Boot and recover without a restart
The app starts and serves while Kill Bill, Mailpit or MinIO is unreachable and resumes using each service when it returns, without a restart, as qualified in Server boundary.

Accounts and server-enforced roles
Visitors create accounts, everyone signs in with a session cookie, and the server enforces the role table in Business rules on every endpoint.

Programme in festival time
The public programme lists published and cancelled sessions with UTC instants, Brussels local times with offsets, festival day and live seats remaining.

Programme Lattice camera
The hero lattice performs the opening camera move, pointer tilt and scroll-linked flight through the day-slabs described in Motion and effects, and reverses step by step when the visitor scrolls back.

Lattice and filters live in the URL
Choosing a day, venue or discipline in the lattice, its control grid or the schedule filters re-filters the list, updates the URL query and announces the count, and a reload, shared link, back or forward restores the same selection and list.

Clash-aware agenda
Visitors keep an agenda that survives reload, and agenda sessions that overlap in real time show clash markers on both schedule rows and a seam in the lattice, including across the clock change.

Keyboard-complete planning and purchase
Filtering, agenda changes, clash resolution and the whole checkout work with the keyboard alone, with visible focus, a checkout dialog that keeps focus inside it, Escape to close and focus returned to the opener.

Plan a festival visit
A visitor filters the programme, builds an agenda, resolves a clash and opens checkout with the agenda's seats held and passes suggested.

Seat holds expire on the server
A seat hold lasts the hold period set by `HOLD_SECONDS`, and the server treats it as expired and releases its seats from its expiry instant on.

Last seat has exactly one winner
When several visitors try to hold the last seat at once, exactly one hold succeeds and every other request gets the sold-out answer that offers the waitlist.

Seats remaining stays exact
Seats remaining always equals capacity minus active holds, open waitlist offers and seats on pending, sold or transferred lines, after every hold, sale, transfer, claim, expiry, refund and cancellation.

Waitlist offers and claim windows
A freed seat goes to the earliest waiting visitor as a mailed offer with a claim window set by `WAITLIST_CLAIM_SECONDS`, and a lapsed offer passes to the next person in line.

From sold out to a waitlist seat
A visitor who misses the last seat joins the waitlist, gets the offer mail when a seat frees, claims it and completes checkout.

Idempotent checkout
Replaying a checkout with the same idempotency key returns the original response with one order and one Kill Bill authorisation, and reusing the key with a different body is refused, as stated in Business rules.

Prices and exact discount allocation
Order amounts follow the price policy, and the group discount and voucher are allocated across lines by the published rule so line shares sum exactly to the cent.

Checkout commits everywhere or nowhere
A full-rate checkout keeps its order, Kill Bill authorisation and capture, stored passes and queued mail together; a reduced-rate checkout keeps its order, uncaptured authorisation and queued mail, storing passes only at approval; a group checkout keeps its order, Kill Bill invoice, stored passes and queued mail; otherwise none remain and no live Kill Bill charge or open invoice is left, as qualified in Business rules.

Confirmation mail and pass PDF
Each order sends one confirmation mail to the buyer with a single stable Message-ID as qualified in Services, and each pass is a stored PDF with a QR code that shows only the holder, item, time, venue and pass code.

Honest pending states during outages
While Mailpit, MinIO or Kill Bill is down, people see the pending or outage copy from Feedback states, and after recovery queued mail is delivered as one message per event and each pending refund or collection makes one Kill Bill transaction, as qualified in Services.

Buy passes and seats
A signed-in visitor holds seats, adds passes, applies a voucher, pays and finds the order, its passes and its confirmation mail.

Private, checked proof documents
Proof uploads are judged by content and size, stored privately in MinIO and readable only by box-office staff through short-lived signed links.

Capture on approval, void on rejection
A reduced-rate order stays authorised until box-office staff decide, then Kill Bill captures it on approval or voids it on rejection, and the buyer gets the matching mail.

Proof hold lapses to a void
When the decision period set by `PROOF_DECISION_SECONDS` ends without approval, the server voids the authorisation, never captures it, and refuses a late decision.

Buy at the reduced rate
A student checks out at the reduced rate, uploads proof, and sees the order confirmed with passes after box-office approval.

Ticket transfer reissues the pass
Transferring a paid ticket issues a new pass to the recipient with no new charge, and the old pass is refused at the door from that moment.

Forwarded copies stay private
Pass PDFs and transfer mails never carry the buyer's email, proof document, rate eligibility, prices, voucher code or payment references.

Door admission rules
Door scans admit a day pass once per festival day, a full-festival pass once per session and a seat ticket once at its own session, and refuse everything else with a stated reason.

Festival day from 05:00 to 05:00
Admission and the daily admissions report count each session against the festival day that runs from 05:00 to 05:00 Brussels time, whatever the browser's or server's time zone.

Transfer a seat and get in
A buyer transfers a seat to a friend, the friend's new pass is admitted at the door, and the buyer's old pass is refused.

Programme state machine
Sessions and artwork entries move only along the legal transitions in Business rules, each recorded in an attributed state history, and every other move is refused.

Publishing at the scheduled instant
A scheduled session or entry reads as published, and appears in the public programme or gallery, from its publishing instant on.

Session times across the clock change
Session and publishing times entered as Brussels wall time resolve by the published rule for the repeated hour, and agenda order, durations and clashes use real instants.

Stale edits are refused
Saving a session or the price policy over a newer version is refused and keeps the newer version.

Curate and publish a session
A curator drafts a session, sends it to review, schedules it and sees it appear in the programme at its publishing time.

Artwork entries stay with their artist
Artists create, edit and submit only their own entries, and another artist's entry is not found on any route and never appears in their lists.

Artwork images private until published
Artwork images are judged by content and size, kept private, shown to curators and their artist through short-lived links, and served publicly only once the entry is published.

Submit an artwork entry
An artist writes an entry, uploads an image, submits it, and sees it in the public gallery once a curator publishes it.

Refunds return only the affected lines
A curator cancellation or a finance refund returns exactly the affected lines of each order, card share to Kill Bill and voucher share to the voucher, summing to the cent, with one notice listing only those items.

Gift voucher ledger
Every voucher movement is a pair of equal debit and credit entries, entries are never edited, and a voucher's balance always equals its entries.

Cancel a performance
A curator cancels a session that sits on several mixed orders, and each affected buyer sees only the cancelled item refunded while their other items stay valid.

Group checkout on invoice
A group booker's checkout of named tickets applies the group discount and issues a Kill Bill invoice with one item per ticket, as qualified in Business rules.

Organisation-scoped detail pages
Group bookers see only their own organisation's orders, invoices and credit notes, and every other id is not found.

Organisation-scoped totals, search and export
Dashboard totals, attendee search and the CSV export are computed on the server from the caller's organisation only.

Book for a class
A teacher books a class into a workshop, sees the invoice and attendees on the dashboard and exports the list.

Invoice collection on the due date
When an invoice falls due the server collects it through Kill Bill and marks it paid, keeping it issued and retrying while Kill Bill is down.

Returned payments, retries and write-off
A recorded bank return marks the invoice payment failed and schedules the retries in Business rules, and a return after the last retry writes the invoice off in Kill Bill.

Credit notes for cancelled group lines
Cancelling or refunding lines of a group order issues one credit note with a Kill Bill item adjustment per line and mails it to the group booker.

Reconciliation with attributed resolutions
A reconciliation run lists every mismatch between Kill Bill transactions and the app's payment records, and finance resolves each one with a note attributed to them.

Close the books
A finance operator runs reconciliation, finds the mismatch left by a charge entered directly in Kill Bill outside the app, resolves it with a note and sees the resolution in the audit trail.

Venues, edition and price policies
Admins manage venues, edition dates and price policies, and changed prices apply to orders placed after the change.

Attributed audit trail
Every staff state change and every automatic publish, expiry, collection and retry writes one audit entry naming its actor.

Responsive layout and display scale
Every screen fits 375×812, 768×1024 and 1280×800 without horizontal overflow, and the hero title and section heads follow the display scale in Visual design.

Loud, exact visual identity
Sections swap the four ground-and-ink pairings, oversized display words overlap masked artwork frames, and schedules, seat counts and prices sit in a ruled grid with equal-width figures.

Contrast, focus and target size
Text contrast, focus rings and tap target sizes meet the limits in Visual design on every section ground.

Named motion, no idle loops
Section heads, the pinned story, the horizontal gallery, ticket rows and dialogs move only as described in Motion and effects, and nothing animates while the visitor is idle except the named exceptions.

Reduced-motion and no-WebGL equivalents
With reduced motion on or WebGL unavailable, the static lattice drawing, toggle grid, stacked story and wrapping gallery replace the moving versions, and every filter and purchase step still works.

Real lattice from programme data
The lattice, its static drawing and the gallery artwork frames are drawn from live programme and entry data by real WebGL, SVG or canvas code, with no screenshots, video or hard-coded state.
`/app/run.json` exists with exactly the string keys `_schema` (value `run-manifest-v1`), `install`, `build` and `serve`.

`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every shipped package with its name, version and licence, plus every bundled font and asset. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`.
Every shipped package is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0. Fonts are OFL-1.1, and other assets are CC0-1.0 or original to the app.
Persistent state lives only in Postgres (records), MinIO (files) and Kill Bill (billing). There is no SQLite, Redis, local-disk state or extra datastore.
The provided service definitions and their dev credentials are not edited, and no service is added.
Server and browser code is TypeScript, and the running app makes no requests to third-party hosts. Fonts, scripts and images are served by the app itself.
Seeded records keep the ids, names, emails and amounts listed in Seed data.
